what_title: From scattered data to useful information
what_lead: Brazil's public data exists, but it is spread across dozens of portals, each with its own format and its own way of downloading. Guaraci fetches everything straight from the official source and delivers it in one place, with quality, integrity and fidelity to the original data.
what_w1: Each dataset sits on a different government portal.
what_w2: Technical formats that are hard to open (such as .dbc files).
what_w3: You have to repeat the download state by state, year by year.
what_w4: It is easy to end up with outdated data or data from intermediaries.
what_s1: No more hunting across dozens of different portals.
what_s2: Delivered ready to use: CSV, Parquet or a database.
what_s3: You choose the period, state and slice, and it downloads everything.
what_s4: Always from the official source, with no intermediaries.

area_pop_p: Population estimates, the Census by age and sex, and municipal GDP: the context that gives meaning to the indicators.

area_san_p: National information on water, sewage and sanitation services, a basis for assessing inequalities and risks.
area_ter_p: All areas can be crossed by municipality, state and region, which makes it possible to compare local realities across Brazil.

faq.q: Is Guaraci free? Do I need to sign up?
faq.a: Yes, it is free and open source, under the MIT license. There is no sign-up or password: you download the project from GitHub and run it on your own machine. Some external sources may require an access key of their own (such as NASA), and the documentation says which ones.

faq.q: Do I need to know how to code?
faq.a: No. After installation, everything happens in a web interface in the browser: you choose the source, fill in filters in a form and follow the download. The terminal is only used in the installation steps, and the step-by-step guide above shows exactly what to type.

faq.q: What do I need to have installed?
faq.a: Git and Docker Desktop, both free. This is the officially supported way to run Guaraci on your machine, and Docker ensures everything works the same on any computer.

faq.q: Does Guaraci host the data or download it from the source?
faq.a: It downloads from the source. Guaraci keeps no copy of the data of its own and is not an intermediary: when you ask for a dataset, it goes to the official system that produces it (DATASUS, the Ministry of Health's open catalog, IBGE, NASA or gov.br). What you receive is the official data, as up to date as the source has published it.

faq.q: In what format does the data arrive?
faq.a: As CSV, Parquet or a SQLite database, ready to open in any analysis tool. This includes the DATASUS datasets distributed as .dbc, an old compressed format that often blocks beginners: Guaraci does the conversion for you.

It is the data lake (a large, always up-to-date data archive) fed by Guaraci. In the future, Sabiá will offer its own query interface, with nothing to install. For now, that interface is under construction; learn more at sabiadatalake.com.br.

faq.q: Can I use the data in research and publications?
faq.a: Yes. This is public data obtained from the official sources, and the terms of use are those of the institution that produces each dataset; we recommend always citing it. Guaraci itself is MIT-licensed and includes a CITATION.cff file in the repository, in case you also want to cite the tool used for the collection.

faq.q: Who are the authors of Guaraci?
faq.a: Luis Felipe Vogel Lopes (lead author, responsible for the current platform), Pedro Guilherme dos Reis Teixeira (original author, creator of the first prototype), Marina Carvalho Arruda Barreto, Bruna Costa de Souza and Bruno Rafael Florentino, and the supervisors Robson Parmezan Bonidia and André Carlos Ponce de Leon Ferreira de Carvalho. The official list, with affiliations, is in the repository's CITATION.cff file.

faq.q: A dataset I need is missing. Can it be added?
faq.a: Yes. The catalog grows with the needs of its users: write to vogel@usp.br saying which dataset you need and the agency that publishes it. The same goes for reporting an error in a collection; the more specific the report, the faster the fix.

docs_desc: Complete Guaraci documentation: installation, web interface, command line and the detailed catalog of the {D} public datasets, with every parameter and field.
docs_og_desc: Installation, web interface, command line and the detailed catalog of Guaraci's public datasets.
docs_lead: From installation to the detail of every field: everything you need to collect official public data, through the web interface or the command line. No rush, no hidden jargon, with each of the {D} datasets documented one by one.
d_ov_1: Guaraci is a public data download orchestrator: it connects directly to the official sources (DATASUS via the microdata FTP, the Ministry of Health's open catalog, IBGE through the SIDRA API, NASA and gov.br, among others) and delivers the data ready to use as CSV, Parquet or SQLite.
d_ov_li1: Primary source, always. Guaraci never fetches from mirrors or third-party curation: each dataset comes from the official system that produces it. You receive the data as up to date as the source has published it, traceable to its origin.
d_ov_li2: Fidelity to the original data. The collection preserves the published content, and converting technical formats (such as DATASUS's .dbc) does not change the values.
d_ov_li3: Docker first. The officially supported path runs in a Docker container, so the environment is identical on any machine, with no dependency conflicts.
d_ov_3: There are two entry points, with the same engine: the web interface (forms in the browser, no code) and the command line guaraci fetch (for automation and scripts). Both read the same parameter schema documented in the catalog.

d_pr_1_a: 500 Internal Server Error or ...docker...ping when running docker build or docker run
d_pr_1_b: Docker Desktop is not ready, not Guaraci. Run .\scripts\desktop\check-docker.cmd (or .sh), which points to the exact item that failed. Usually it is enough to open Docker Desktop and wait for the whale icon to stop saying “Starting...”; if it hangs, restart with wsl --shutdown and open it again.
d_pr_2_a: Port 8002 in use (port is already allocated)
d_pr_2_b: Stop the old container with stop-guaraci or start on another port: powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File scripts/desktop/start-guaraci.ps1 -HostPort 8003.
d_pr_3_a: Interface with no data or “Guaraci UI not found”
d_pr_3_b: Check the volume (-v "${PWD}:/app") and the write permissions of the data/ folder.
d_pr_4_b: The image needs the datasus extra. Rebuild with docker build --no-cache -t guaraci ..
d_pr_5_a: Container exits immediately, with no logs
d_pr_5_b: In manual mode, make sure the -it flag is present.
d_pr_6_b: Inside Docker there is no way to open the host's file explorer: copy the host_output_dir path shown in the interface.
d_pr_7_a: Export requested, but no file generated
d_pr_7_b: The filters probably excluded 100% of the records. Check the logs and the export_warning notice.
d_ui_0: With Guaraci running, the interface is at http://localhost:8002. The whole flow happens on one screen:
d_ui_1: Choose the source. The list has the {E} catalog entries ({D} distinct datasets, plus the alternative routes to the same dataset) with search. Each one exposes its own parameters, and the form builds itself from the schema (the same one documented in the catalog).
d_ui_2: Fill in the basic filters. Period (years), states, groups or diseases, depending on the source. The advanced fields (pagination, alternative URL, raw snapshot) stay collapsed, and the defaults suit most cases.
d_ui_3: Choose the export format. CSV (opens in Excel), Parquet (data analysis) or SQLite (local database). With no format, Guaraci only collects and records the manifest.
d_ui_4: Create the download and follow it. The progress bar and live log show each file being fetched, validated and converted. Jobs stay in the history, so you can repeat or debug them later.
d_ui_5: Open the result. The files go to the Guaraci Downloads folder (on the Desktop, by default), together with a manifest.json describing the collection.
d_ui_call: For large DATASUS sources (SIA, SIH, CNES), use the discovery preflight before downloading: it counts the files by group and state without transferring anything, in the interface or with guaraci fetch discover.
d_cli_0: The guaraci fetch group reaches any registered source with four subcommands. Inside Docker, prefix it with docker run --rm -v "${PWD}:/app" guaraci (or use the interactive shell).
d_cli_3_p: Available for SIH and the eleven DATASUS FTP microdata systems (SIA, CNES, SINASC and so on): it counts files by group and state without downloading anything. With --sizes, it also adds up the total size. SIM and SINAN resolve their files internally during collection and are left out of the preflight.
d_cli_r1: --set KEY=VALUE is automatically converted to the type declared in the schema (integer, boolean, list).
d_cli_r2: Omit --format to collect without exporting (only the manifest is written).
d_cli_r3: -o FOLDER changes the destination (default: Guaraci Downloads on the Desktop).
d_cli_r4: NASA credentials are never flags, only environment variables (section 5).
d_cli_end: Each source in the catalog comes with a fetch run example ready to copy.
d_out_csv: Open in Excel or LibreOffice and share with people who do not code.
d_out_pq: Data analysis (pandas, polars, R, Spark): compact and fast, preserves types.
d_out_sq: Local SQL queries with no server, in a single .db file.
d_out_l1: manifest.json: every collection writes a manifest with source, parameters, files and timestamps, which is the data's provenance record.
d_out_l2: keep_raw=true: besides the export, saves the raw snapshot (raw/*.jsonl for APIs) for auditing.
d_out_l3: export_warning: if the filters zero out the records or pagination truncates (max_pages), the notice appears in the manifest and the logs. It is the first place to look when “nothing came back”.
d_out_l4: Source formats: DATASUS .dbc and .DBF files are decoded automatically, and you never need to deal with them.
d_cred_0: Almost everything in Guaraci needs no sign-up. The exceptions are two NASA sources, and the keys are free:
d_cred_1: nasa_power and all IBGE, OpenDataSUS, DATASUS and gov.br sources require no credential. For safety, keys are read only from the environment: they never become a job parameter and are never written to a manifest.
d_orch_0: For those who maintain a continuous archive (such as the Sabiá data lake), guaraci orchestrate automates collection in two bronze layers:
d_orch_l1: raw/: the raw official file, at the source's native granularity (annual SINAN stays annual; monthly SIH stays monthly).
d_orch_l2: refined/: the same rows repartitioned into the uniform tree source/group/state/year/month, sliced by event date.
d_orch_1: Commands: orchestrate profiles (cadence of each source), plan (dry run), backfill (full history), update (only the delta, driven by a CSV ledger) and status. The scripts/server/orchestrate.{sh,ps1} wrappers, ready for cron, handle locking and logging. Details are in docs/ORCHESTRATOR.md in the repository.
d_best_1: Start small. Use the shortest time window and the narrowest filters possible, and widen them once the flow is validated.
d_best_2: Measure before downloading. For large FTP sources (SIA, SIH, CNES), run fetch discover first, because broad selections can resolve to thousands of files and many gigabytes.
d_best_3: Export only when you need to. Set output_format only when you want the final dataset; collection without export is faster and is already recorded.
d_best_4: Watch the export_warning. It flags empty exports and truncated pagination.
d_best_5: Current-year data is partial. DATASUS sources accept the current year, but publication lags by about 2 to 3 months, so compare with care.
d_best_6: Cite the official source. The terms of use are those of the producing institution; Guaraci ships a CITATION.cff in case you also want to cite the tool.
